nodes.summary: For any finite measure, the probability that the origin is connected to the boundary of the box of radius `n` inside the box tends to the percolation probability.
nodes.title: Box-boundary connection probability tends to percolation probability

nodes.summary: The event `{x ↔ ∞}` that the open cluster of `x` is infinite.
nodes.title: Event that the open cluster of a site is infinite

nodes.summary: A connection from the origin to a site outside the box passes through the box boundary.
nodes.title: A connection to outside the box passes through the box boundary

nodes.summary: For any finite measure, the probability that the origin is connected to the complement of the box of radius `n - 1` tends to the percolation probability.
nodes.title: Crossing probabilities converge to the percolation probability

nodes.summary: With at most one infinite cluster almost surely, `μ(x ↔ ∞, y ↔ ∞) ≤ μ(x ↔ y)`.
nodes.title: Joint percolation at most connectivity given no two infinite clusters

nodes.summary: The two-point connectivity `μ(x ↔ y)` of a measure on bond configurations of `ℤ^d`.
nodes.title: Two-point connectivity of a bond measure on $\mathbb{Z}^d$

nodes.summary: Without percolation, the two-point connectivity from the origin tends to zero uniformly: for every `ε > 0` there is `n` with `μ(0 ↔ x) < ε` for all `x` outside the box of radius `n`.
nodes.title: Uniform decay of two-point connectivity without percolation

nodes.summary: If `μ` satisfies the FKG inequality for the events `{x ↔ ∞}` (`hPA`), is translation invariant on them (`hTI`), has at most one infinite cluster almost surely (`huniq`), and percolates (`htheta`), then `μ(0 ↔ x) ≥ θ²` for every `x`.
nodes.title: Two-point lower bound from FKG, invariance, uniqueness and percolation

nodes.summary: If `x` and `y` both lie in infinite clusters, either they are connected or there are at least two infinite clusters.
nodes.title: Disconnected sites in infinite clusters give two infinite clusters

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
